transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining today's project huddle. As we all know, the school has approved the concept of building a twelve-bed teaching garden beside the science wing, and I have final authority to approve the construction, purchasing, and safety plan before we move forward. The current draft plan is on the table — in-ground beds, October 18 workday, $3,000 from general funds, and standard latex gardening gloves. Before I can sign off on this campus project plan, I need each of you to report any requirements you have verified regarding the site, purchasing, and student safety. Let's go around the room. Could the science teacher, facilities coordinator, business manager, and school nurse each share what you've confirmed?

transcript.text: I need to report a site safety issue. I just received a soil test result yesterday from the proposed garden area — it measured lead at 180 parts per million. Our district garden standard requires removing the top six inches of soil and using raised beds at that reading. This means the current draft plan's in-ground beds would not meet the district standard. I received this result after the draft plan was circulated and haven't yet entered it in the project folder, so I'm flagging it now.

transcript.text: I need to report a site requirement from the facilities side. My utility-locate request just cleared this morning, and the site is approved for work starting October 28 — not before that date. Facilities policy also requires a posted site permit before any excavation or bed assembly can begin. The locate response arrived after the draft workday of October 18 was already proposed, so that date will not work. We'll need to move the workday to October 28 or later, and ensure the site permit is posted before any ground work begins.

transcript.text: I need to report a student safety requirement. I just completed my student health review this week, after the draft equipment list was prepared, and I identified a documented severe latex allergy among the students scheduled for garden instruction. Under our school safety protocol, this requires nitrile-only gloves — no latex gloves — and an allergy-safety notice posted at the garden entrance. The current draft plan lists standard latex gardening gloves, which would not be safe for these students. This needs to be updated before the plan can be approved.
